$comment: Machine-readable project state. The human-readable companion is MEMORY.md; keep the two in agreement. Validated by scripts/check-memory-freshness.sh in CI.
next_task: Fix the budget-check race (apps/gateway/src/middleware/budget.rs::check() is not atomic under concurrency -- proven, 8/8 runs, see the session 5 audit and the #[ignore]'d concurrent_requests_can_overshoot_a_hard_budget test). Then populate FallbackChain's alternates at its production call site (routes/openai_compat.rs, currently hardcoded to &[]). Then spawn workers::reconciliation::run and the budget-alert worker in main.rs. Full priority order: MEMORY.md 'Next Steps' / audit artifact section 16.

audit.method: direct code tracing + 4 parallel focused investigations + adversarial tests actually executed, not documentation review

phases.name: Foundation
phases.evidence: Workspace, full schema migrations with monthly partitioning, typed config, CI, health endpoints verified against a running gateway, ADRs 001-007 (007 added session 5, Vertex AI JWT signing).

phases.name: Auth, keys, orgs
phases.evidence: argon2id auth, sessions, API key CRUD with LRU+Redis+PG tiers, audit log, org/member management, dashboard signup/login/keys pages. 14+ integration tests written (run in CI). Session 5 note: API keys meant for inference traffic can read broad org-wide management/billing data via require_reader endpoints -- not a cross-tenant leak, but a wider read boundary than an 'inference key' implies, with no scoping mechanism to narrow it.

phases.name: Core gateway
phases.evidence: Ten provider adapters (Vertex AI added session 5), full twelve-stage pipeline, rate limiting (proven atomic -- 50 racing callers against a limit of 10 admit exactly 10), budgets, BYOK, shared key pool, usage worker, Prometheus metrics, Grafana dashboard. Session 5: fixed an SSRF vulnerability (BYOK base_url reaching cloud metadata from a zero-privilege signup) and a silent metering-completeness bug (the one metric built to detect billing loss couldn't, because usage::emit's Result was discarded).
remaining: Budget checking is not atomic under concurrency -- proven, not theorised. budget::check() reads spend and compares to the limit; the counter increments later, separately. Reproduced 8/8 runs under genuine multi-thread parallelism: 20 concurrent requests against a $1.00 hard limit with $0.05 headroom admitted 2-5 (15-45% overshoot). Applies identically to all four budget scopes (key/team/region/org). Fix needs a reserve-then-true-up or atomic increment-check-rollback redesign matching the rate limiter's already-proven pattern. This is the single highest-priority open finding from the session 5 audit (P0-01).
No idempotency key is sent to any upstream provider on retry -- a retried timeout can silently double-bill Aegis's own provider account (not the customer).

phases.name: Optimization engine
phases.evidence: Classifier 98% on 100 labelled fixtures, router with conservative defaults, exact cache, compressor. verify-phase.sh 3 passes. Semantic cache (cache/semantic.rs, 624 lines, 15 tests, Qdrant-backed) is fully implemented and tested but -- found by a session 3 audit -- was never called from the live pipeline. Session 5 audit found the fallback chain and streaming resilience have the same 'built but not effectively wired' shape.
remaining: Wire cache/semantic.rs into the pipeline -- a product decision (adds embedding-API latency to every cache-miss request) as much as a code change.

Populate FallbackChain's alternates parameter at its one production call site (routes/openai_compat.rs, hardcoded to &[] today). Combined with the router's never-downgrade guarantee, complex/passthrough requests get zero cross-provider redundancy -- chain length collapses to 1, proven by the codebase's own test. Session 5 audit finding P0-04.

Streaming (stream_chat/stream_messages) has no retry, no fallback, and never calls state.health.record_success/record_failure -- the circuit breaker never learns from streaming traffic. Session 5 audit finding P1-01.
Add an outer request timeout at the router level -- currently unbounded, up to ~90s (360s for reasoning models) per fallback-chain entry with no outer deadline anywhere in the stack.

phases.name: Dashboards, billing, launch prep
phases.evidence: Stripe webhook verification, invoice assembly with an independent fee-consistency check, budget enforcement (single-request blocking genuinely works; see phase 2 for the concurrency caveat), admin console, landing page, docs, savings CSV export, runbooks. All 12 dashboard pages built and browser-verified. tests/overhead_under_load.rs measures real pipeline overhead under 64-way concurrency: P99 1.27ms on a debug build -- gateway overhead only, explicitly excludes provider time.
remaining: P4.8 EXECUTE infra/loadtest/k6-gateway.js against a deployed instance (1k RPS over a real network + database) -- the in-process concurrency test is real evidence but is a narrower claim. Session 5: TTFT, tokens/sec, and provider-to-provider comparisons also remain unmeasured -- none possible without live provider accounts.

P4.2 budget alert delivery (email, Slack webhook) -- workers/budget_alerts.rs is implemented and tested but never called from any live path, and (found session 5) never spawned as a worker in main.rs at all.

phases.name: Launch + provider expansion
phases.evidence: All five original expansion providers tested. Classifier v2 trained via a real dump/fit pipeline. Status page endpoint. Launch playbook written. Weekly digest sent by workers/scheduler.rs with a distributed claim (64-way concurrency test proves exactly one replica ever wins a period). Referral program. CHANGELOG.md written. Session 5: Vertex AI (Google Cloud) added as a tenth provider -- service-account JWT auth, delegates request/response handling to the existing google.rs adapter, 14 tests, docs/adr/0007-vertex-ai-jwt-signing.md. Not yet verified against a real GCP project (no service account key supplied).

phases.name: Enterprise readiness
phases.evidence: Offline license validation with grace period, SCIM 2.0 shapes handling both Okta and Entra deprovisioning, SSO assertion validation logic correct and tested (audience/issuer/expiry/replay), per-tenant HKDF keys, region pinning enforcement genuinely wired (session 3). Compliance pack written and corrected session 5 (security whitepaper's content_capture claim didn't match the code -- fixed). Read replica routing live. Self-hosted docker-compose + web Dockerfile added.
remaining: SSO cannot functionally complete -- found session 5. Assertion validation is correct, but sso_start builds a callback to /api/auth/sso/callback and that route is never registered anywhere in the router. A real login has nowhere to land. Small fix once the callback handler's own completeness is confirmed.
Verify SSO/SCIM against a real Okta or Entra tenant -- never done, only shape-tested, and SSO can't complete end to end yet regardless (see above).
TOTP: algorithm is correct and tested but has no repo layer, no enrollment endpoint, and no login-time verification -- 2FA cannot actually be turned on today.
SCIM tokens have no self-service provisioning route -- correctly built and isolated, but mintable only by a direct database write.

phases.name: Scale + moat
phases.evidence: UCB1 outcome bandit with a 3000-step replay showing it beats static routing in a standalone simulation -- the live router records outcomes into the bandit but never reads it back to make a routing decision, so it has zero effect on production traffic today (session 3 finding, re-confirmed session 5 by reading engine/router.rs directly). TypeScript and Python SDKs, both verified. Regional budgets. Nightly pricing-drift job. Spend anomaly detection. Cost-center chargeback. Investor pack. Session 5: a session-5 audit found Postgres connection-pool math (N replicas x 20 connections against the reference instance's connection cap) hard-limits the fleet to roughly 8-10 replicas with zero headroom, independent of Redis or CPU -- the first real scaling wall.
remaining: Wire the bandit's learned policy back into engine/router.rs's routing decision -- currently write-only.
A connection-pooling proxy (PgBouncer or equivalent) or a larger reference instance class is needed before scaling meaningfully past ~10 replicas -- neither exists in this codebase today.

blockers.summary: Docker Desktop was not functional on the build machine as of session 3 (installer fragments only, no docker.exe, no daemon). Not re-checked session 5.
blockers.impact: Nothing has been verified against live Postgres, Redis, or Qdrant. Integration tests compile and skip locally; CI runs them against service containers. Session 5 finding: even in CI, no test reads the Redis env var CI provisions -- every concurrency proof (rate limiter, scheduler claim, the new budget-race proof) has only ever run against store::MemoryStore, never real Redis.
blockers.workaround: Reinstall Docker Desktop from scratch and confirm with `docker version` (not a directory listing) before assuming it works. The gateway compiles and unit-tests with no external service in the meantime.

blockers.summary: No real provider API key has been supplied for any provider, including the newly-added Vertex AI (which needs a GCP service-account JSON key, not an API key).
blockers.impact: The pipeline is verified against a mock provider only. TTFT, tokens/sec, and any real cross-provider performance comparison remain entirely unmeasured -- not estimated, not claimed.
blockers.workaround: Add one key (Gemini) and one GCP service account (Vertex) and send a single request each; the savings figure and Vertex's live token exchange can then be checked for real.

launch_blockers.summary: budget::check() is not atomic under concurrency -- proven with real numbers, session 5. 20 concurrent requests against a $1.00 hard limit with $0.05 headroom admitted 2-5 of them (15-45% overshoot) in 8 of 8 runs under genuine multi-thread parallelism. Applies to all four budget scopes.
launch_blockers.impact: A customer's stated hard spending ceiling is not reliably enforced under exactly the condition (bursty/concurrent/retried traffic) it exists to protect against.
launch_blockers.action: Redesign to a reserve-then-true-up or atomic increment-check-rollback model, matching the rate limiter's already-proven atomic Lua-script pattern. See apps/gateway/src/middleware/budget.rs::concurrent_requests_can_overshoot_a_hard_budget for the reproduction.

launch_blockers.summary: 9 of the priced models remain marked UNVERIFIED (mistral x2, groq x2, moonshot/kimi-k2, google/gemini-1.5-flash, google/gemini-1.5-pro, vertex/gemini-3.6-flash, vertex/gemini-3.1-pro-preview). Separately and more importantly (session 5): no provider's pricing accounts for cached tokens at all, and Gemini 2.5 Pro's 200K-token pricing tier isn't modeled.
launch_blockers.impact: Every savings figure and invoice line for the 9 unverified models depends on unconfirmed numbers. Any customer using prompt caching (a common pattern, not an edge case) gets a wrong actual_cost today -- Anthropic under-counted, OpenAI over-counted.
launch_blockers.action: Follow docs/runbooks/pricing-update.md for the 9 remaining rows. Separately, add a cached-token dimension to TokenUsage and a cache-rate pair to ModelPricing -- a schema-level fix, not a table update. Verify with: grep -c 'UNVERIFIED.to_string()' apps/gateway/src/metering/pricing.rs (must read 0).

launch_blockers.summary: FallbackChain::build's alternates parameter is hardcoded to &[] at its one production call site (routes/openai_compat.rs). Combined with the router's never-downgrade guarantee, complex/passthrough requests get zero cross-provider redundancy and no outer request timeout bounds the resulting hang (up to ~90-360s).
launch_blockers.impact: A routine provider hiccup -- not even severe enough to trip the 5-failure circuit breaker -- can hang exactly the highest-value requests for minutes with total failure and no fallback.
launch_blockers.action: Populate alternates from the pricing table's cross-provider equivalents at the call site; add an outer request timeout at the router level. The FallbackChain logic itself is already built and tested.

launch_blockers.summary: infra/loadtest/k6-gateway.js has never been executed against a deployed instance. tests/overhead_under_load.rs provides real in-process evidence (P99 1.27ms, 64-way concurrency, mock provider, debug build) but this excludes network, real DB/Redis contention, and does not reach 1k RPS.
launch_blockers.impact: The sub-1ms P99 overhead claim on the landing page is partially substantiated (gateway overhead only), not purely a design target, but the full production-conditions claim and any TTFT/tokens-per-second/provider-comparison claim remain entirely unverified.
launch_blockers.action: Deploy to staging and run infra/loadtest/k6-gateway.js; record the measured P99 before repeating any performance claim under production-network conditions.

launch_blockers.summary: No backup has ever been taken, so none has ever been restored.
launch_blockers.impact: An untested backup is not a backup. Also the largest gap flagged in docs/compliance/soc2-readiness.md (Availability criterion A1.3).
launch_blockers.action: Run scripts/backup-restore-drill.sh once a database exists and record the result in MEMORY.md.

fixed_this_session.summary: A zero-privilege free-tier signup could register a BYOK provider with base_url pointed at 169.254.169.254 (cloud metadata); the gateway's own credential-test endpoint would issue the request server-side. Fixed with middleware/ssrf_guard.rs (resolve-then-classify against loopback/RFC1918/link-local/CGN/IPv6-unique-local/IPv4-mapped-IPv6), wired into create_provider. Proven closed by a new integration test against the real handler and a real database. Residual, documented risk: validation-time not connect-time, so DNS rebinding is not fully closed.

usage::emit's Result was discarded at all three call sites in routes/openai_compat.rs, so the Prometheus metric built to detect 'served but never billed' incremented regardless of whether the write actually succeeded. Fixed to gate the metric on success and log failures with context; stream failures now carry a real error_type.

docs/compliance/security-whitepaper.md described content_capture as an opt-in, encrypted content-storage control. It is dead code; only zero_retention gates anything, and the exact-match cache stores plaintext content in Redis for 24h by default. Corrected in the document with the correction left visible.

verification.concurrency_overhead_p99_ms_observed_ran: 0.58-1.27 across 3 runs (session 2 x1, session 5 x2) -- debug build, shared build-machine hardware, no isolation from other load; treat as a range, not a constant
